content: 1. In May 2005, Smith GCS and Pell JP conducted a systematic review of randomized controlled trials to evaluate the use of parachutes in preventing death and major trauma caused by gravitational challenges, as published in the BMJ in 2003 (Volume 327, Pages 1459–1461). 2. The ICECI Coordination and Development Group provided an open document on May 18, 2005, detailing their findings. 3. Aeromedical transport was discussed in the fourth edition of Wilderness Medicine: Management of Wilderness and Environmental Emergencies, edited by Auerbach PS and published by Mosby in St. Louis, MO, in 2001 (Pages 660–672). Gearhart PA, Wuerz R, and Localio AR analyzed the cost-effectiveness of helicopter emergency medical services (EMS) for trauma patients in the Annals of Emergency Medicine in 1997 (Volume 30, Pages 500–506). 4. Nicholl J and colleagues published a PDF on March 11, 2005, discussing the impact of terrorist bombings in Madrid, as reported in Critical Care in 2005 (Volume 9, Pages 20–260). Frykberg ER explored the medical management of disasters and mass casualties from terrorist bombings in the Journal of Trauma in 2002 (Volume 53, Pages 201–212) and shared lessons learned from Belfast to Beirut in the Annals of Surgery in 1988 (Volume 208, Pages 569–576). 5. Cone DC and colleagues reviewed field triage systems and methodologies in the literature, as published in Prehospital Emergency Care in 2004 (Volume 8, Pages 130–137). 6. The American College of Surgeons' Committee on Trauma outlined resources for optimal care of injured patients in a 1999 publication from Chicago, IL. They emphasized the importance of prehospital and emergency room management in urban Latin America, as discussed in the Journal of Trauma in 1995 (Volume 39, Pages 457–462). Trauma mortality patterns across nations with varying economic levels were analyzed in the Journal of Trauma in 1998 (Volume 44, Pages 804–812). 7. Joshipura M and colleagues highlighted the need for strengthening trauma systems globally in Essential Trauma Care, published in Injury in 2004 (Volume 35, Pages 841–845). Mock C, Joshipura M, and Goosen J further discussed global improvements in trauma care in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2004 (Volume 82, Page 241). 8. Ali J and colleagues demonstrated improved trauma outcomes following the implementation of the Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS) program in a developing country, as reported in the Journal of Trauma in 1993 (Volume 34, Pages 898–899). The impact of the Prehospital Trauma Life Support (PHTLS) program on prehospital trauma care was analyzed in the Journal of Trauma in 1997 (Volume 42, Pages 786–790). 9. The American College of Emergency Physicians and the American College of Surgeons published a PDF on March 11, 2005, with recommendations for life-supporting first aid training for the lay public in disaster preparedness, as discussed by Angus DC and colleagues in Prehospital Disaster Medicine in 1993 (Volume 8, Pages 157–160). 10. Bazzoli GJ identified key barriers and facilitating factors in community-based trauma system development in the Journal of Trauma in 1999 (Volume 47, Supplement 3, Pages S22–S24). 11. The complexity of comparing different EMS systems in Europe was explored in a survey published in the Annals of Emergency Medicine in 1993 (Volume 22, Pages 99–102). Campbell JE authored Basic Trauma Life Support for Paramedics and Other Advanced Providers, fourth edition, published by Brady/Prentice Hall Health in Upper Saddle River, NJ, in 2000. 12. Carney CJ provided a UK perspective on prehospital care in the British Medical Bulletin in 1999 (Volume 55, Pages 757–766). Chawla R emphasized the need for trauma care programs in developing countries in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 1999 (Volume 77, Pages 948–949). 13. Coats TJ and Davies G discussed prehospital care for road traffic casualties in the British Medical Journal in 2002 (Volume 324, Pages 1135–1141). The European Transport Safety Council published a PDF on May 18, 2005, addressing related issues. 14. Feero S and colleagues examined the effect of out-of-hospital time on trauma survival in the American Journal of Emergency Medicine in 1995 (Volume 13, Pages 133–135). Fiander S published a PDF on May 18, 2005, discussing similar topics. 15. Greengross P analyzed the impact of helicopter services on trauma survival as part of a continuum of care in the British Medical Journal in 1995 (Volume 311, Pages 1164–1165). Husum H studied the effects of early prehospital life support for war-injured individuals during the Battle of Jalalabad, Afghanistan, as reported in Prehospital Disaster Medicine in 1999 (Volume 14, Pages 75–80). 16. Trauma care challenges and developments in China were discussed in Injury in 1996 (Volume 27, Pages 471–475). Trauma care systems in India were analyzed in Injury in 2003 (Volume 34, Pages 686–692). 17. Kerr WA, Kerns TJ, and Bissell RA compared mortality rates among trauma patients transported by helicopter versus ambulance in Maryland, as reported in Prehospital Disaster Medicine in 1999 (Volume 14, Pages 159–161). 18. Kirsch TD provided an overview of emergency medicine practices worldwide in the Annals of Emergency Medicine in 1998 (Volume 32, Pages 237–238). Kobusingye O, Guwarrudde D, and Lett R examined injury patterns in rural and urban Uganda in Injury Prevention in 2001 (Volume 7, Pages 46–50). 19. Kuehl A authored the third edition of Prehospital Systems and Medical Oversight, published by Kendall-Hunt Publishing in St. Louis, MO, in 2002. 20. Lenworth MJ and colleagues demonstrated the benefits of prehospital advanced life support in trauma care in the Journal of Trauma in 1984 (Volume 24, Pages 8–13). London JA and colleagues discussed advances and evidence-based practices in prehospital care in the Emergency Medicine Journal in 2003 (Volume 20, Pages 114–115). 21. MacFarlane C and Benn CA evaluated emergency medical service systems and proposed a classification to determine indicators in the Emergency Medicine Journal in 2003 (Volume 20, Pages 188–191). 22. Maheshwari A and colleagues questioned the effectiveness of prehospital ACLS in Emergency Medicine Clinics of North America in 2002 (Volume 20, Pages 759–770). 23. Mock C, Nii-Amon Kotei D, and Maier RV highlighted the low utilization of formal medical services by injured individuals in developing nations, as reported in the Journal of Trauma in 1997 (Volume 42, Pages 504–513). 24. Trauma system development in Ghana was discussed in the Ghana Medical Journal in 2001 (Volume 35, Pages 1–3). Mock C, Arreola-Risa C, and Quansah R examined strengthening care for injured individuals in less developed countries, using Ghana and Mexico as case studies, in Injury Control and Safety Promotion in 2003 (Volume 10, Pages 45–51). 25. Nicholl J analyzed prehospital deaths from accidental injury in the British Medical Journal in 1994 (Volume 309, Page 57). Nicholl J, Brazier JE, and Snooks HA evaluated the effects of London's helicopter emergency medical service on trauma survival in the British Medical Journal in 1995 (Volume 311, Pages 217–222). 26. The cost and benefits of paramedic skills in prehospital trauma care were assessed in Health Technology Assessment in 1998 (Volume 2, Issue 17, Pages 1–72). The cost of injury was discussed in Emergency Medicine Clinics of North America in 1993 (Volume 11, Pages 241–253). 27. Tamburlini G and colleagues evaluated guidelines for emergency triage assessment and treatment in developing countries, as published in the Archives of Disease in Childhood in 1999 (Volume 81, Pages 478–482).
